minutes.headline: Committee heard an FY25 budget gap warning as ESSER ends, tabled class-account funds, and sent petty cash policy back.
minutes.summary: The School Committee heard the first FY25 budget development briefing, in which the superintendent and business manager said the challenge is much larger than the end of ESSER, with cuts coming in nearly every area. It also reviewed the end-of-year report, ESSER status, petty cash accounts, old class accounts and the athletics finances. Votes were taken on minutes, the end-of-year report, the petty cash policy, tabling class accounts, donations and executive session.

attendees.role: central office staff (petty cash), joined by phone/online

public_comment.topic: Thanked citizens and high school student volunteers who provided child care at the special town meeting; suggested starting earlier than 7:00.

votes.motion: Approve regular session minutes of October 18, 2023
Accept the FY23 end of year report for submission to DESE
Send the petty cash policy back to subcommittee, rename and adjust petty cash accounts accordingly, and contact town offices as needed
Table the student activity class accounts question to the next meeting
Accept the float donations with gratitude
Go into executive session at 8:19 p.m. for non-union negotiation strategy and adjourn thereafter

budget_items.what_was_said: The warrant total for the two weeks was read; no line item transfers.

budget_items.topic: FY23 end of year report local spending
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager said local funds spent on educating students were stated for the public.
Roughly this much was spent in revolving accounts and grants including food service and extended day.
The tutor line is overspent; vacant ESSER position, leftover and fringe could offset.
A member noted all but a small amount of the federal money is spent down.
Treasurer requires reconciling petty cash accounts, which would take money from budget lines; limits discussed.
Unclaimed class account balances total over a threshold; staff proposed a scholarship line for trips.
Middle school fee is below expenses; high school fee has not changed; local budget supports some salaries and expenses.
Grants not yet set up in the accounting system so salaries are charged to local lines pending journal entries.
Increase over the 2.5 percent guideline once ESSER positions are rolled in; health insurance, out-of-district tuition, transportation, utilities and technology rising.
The superintendent said the ESSER money lost is much less than the stated gap.

decisions.decision: Petty cash accounts will be kept open and renamed (home economics, school committee, special services); policy goes back to the policy subcommittee.
Chair will draft a letter to legislators about state education funding for the next agenda.
Members to give the superintendent priorities on cuts before the budget is presented.
Capital staffing plan to be presented with the January budget presentation rather than December.
Class account question to return at next meeting with more publicity.

Superintendent report; new finance director hire
FY24 grants and finance office transition

not_audible: Vote counts and results for all motions were not captured; only 'all those in favor' appears.
Several figures such as the warrant total and ESSER deficit are garbled.
The meeting date was identified as FY25 budget by context; captions say FY2/FY4 inconsistently.

what_happened.line: The superintendent and business manager said the FY25 budget challenge is much larger than the end of federal ESSER funding, with cuts expected in nearly every area.
The committee voted to send the petty cash policy back to subcommittee and to keep the petty cash accounts open under new names.
The committee tabled the question of old student class accounts to its next meeting, to return with more publicity.
The committee voted to accept the FY23 end of year report for submission to DESE, and to accept the float donations.
The capital staffing plan will come with the January budget presentation rather than December, and members are to give the superintendent cut priorities beforehand.

why_it_matters: The FY25 school budget is expected to rise above the 2.5 percent guideline as ESSER positions move onto local lines, which bears on what residents are later asked to fund and on which school services face cuts.
Unclaimed balances in old class accounts will return to the committee, so anyone who thinks they have a claim on those funds has until the next meeting to come forward.
watch_next: The next School Committee meeting, where the tabled class accounts question returns.
The January budget presentation, which will include the capital staffing plan.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The four non-procedural votes match, and so do the ESSER loss, the 2.5% increase and the 10% health insurance figure. The main differences are the letter to legislators, which our minutes record as a Chair action and the official minutes record only as a suggestion, and a $1.5 million figure in ours against $1 million in the official minutes.
